video_title: Wembanyama for MVP? Maxime Aubin Says Spurs “Have to Win the Whole Thing” - Around The Beat

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama is working to simplify his isolation game
quotes.excerpt: he wants to do less and do it better and to repeat the same movements again and again
quotes.quote: I was asking Victor Wembanyama about his isolation game. He said during media day that he wanted to really improve his isolation game. I asked him after five games how he feels about it, if he is improving, and in what area. He was basically trying to say that he is trying to simplify his game. This is still a work in progress, as we can see. But I think he is getting better every day and working a lot on this. The whole point was trying for him to say that he wants to do less and do it better and to repeat the same movements again and again. Once again, he is not there yet. I think that is the craziest part about Wembanyama. He can average 35, 10 rebounds, and four blocks, and you watch his offensive game and you are like, it is a mess. We do not understand what is going on. So, he has a lot to improve still, but I think he is heading in the right direction.
quotes.social_post: Victor Wembanyama is working to simplify his offensive game. Maxime Aubin notes that despite his massive stats, Wembanyama is focused on doing less and doing it better to repeat the same movements.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin discusses his recent conversation with Victor Wembanyama regarding his efforts to simplify his isolation game.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama was affected by the criticism following the French league finals
quotes.excerpt: this is still something that hurts him, what happened in the finals
quotes.quote: After the finals, with all the criticism he had, I was really hopeful I could try to talk to him one-on-one, like a lot of other people. Let's say he was very quiet. I talked to his people, to his agents, and they said basically he does not want to talk about the finals. From what I understand now, this is still something that hurts him, what happened in the finals. He does not really want to talk about it yet. One other thing I think that is happening right now for him is that he had the short summer. The NBA finals went all the way to mid-June, then he played for the French national team this summer. So what he told me really recently is that he can have the FOMO a little bit of France. He wished the summer could be longer, just to spend more time there, but also to prepare better for the NBA season.
quotes.social_post: Maxime Aubin reports that Victor Wembanyama is still affected by the criticism following the French league finals and opted not to discuss the series with media.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin explains that Victor Wembanyama is still processing the criticism he received following the French league finals.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama feels a responsibility to use his platform for social issues
quotes.excerpt: he feels really close to the young generation in France and especially to the high schoolers
quotes.quote: The first thing to understand about him is that he feels really close to the young generation in France and especially to the high schoolers who are protesting right now in France. It started with the high schoolers, and not every high schooler in France, but the ones that study in the suburbs of Paris, in public schools, that are underfunded, they do not have enough money, they do not have enough teachers. Anyway, when he talked about it, he was outspoken about it, why? Because he said it himself, I was the same kid who went to a public high school in the suburbs of Paris. So he said I experienced the same thing than they do. So that is why I guess he feels so into it. Knowing him, he is so intelligent, so smart, so mature, that he has a voice. I mean, he realizes that he has a big voice, and he has smart things to do and to say about it.
quotes.social_post: Victor Wembanyama is using his platform to speak out on social issues in France, specifically regarding underfunded public schools, drawing on his own experiences growing up in the Paris suburbs.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin describes how Victor Wembanyama uses his platform to support students in French public schools.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' starting lineup changes are a work in progress
quotes.excerpt: it looks really different because of what they decided to do, to start this three-guard lineup
quotes.quote: It looks really different. You said it, it looks the same because there is only one more player, maybe two, the draftees. But it looks really different because of what they decided to do, to start this three-guard lineup with Jeremy Sochan in the starting five. I think it is a lot of change. Like we have seen in the couple first games, it is still a work in progress. They are very confident it is going to work. From what we see, it is a tough one for many reasons, so we will see if it works or not. What I am seeing, I am seeing a lot of confidence. I do not want to say overconfidence, but you know, I just feel like they are so confident on themselves that they are going to be amazing and that these five starters are going to work together and be amazing.
quotes.social_post: The Spurs are committed to their new three-guard starting lineup featuring Jeremy Sochan. Maxime Aubin notes the team remains confident in the strategy despite it being a work in progress.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin analyzes the Spurs' decision to implement a three-guard starting lineup featuring Jeremy Sochan.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox is bouncing back well after his injury
quotes.excerpt: I think if you see the five first games of the season right now, he is one of the best Spurs players
quotes.quote: I think we have all been very tough on him. Just to put things in perspective, they went all the way to the finals also because of him, first thing. They lost the finals, okay, it was bad in the finals, this is true. He was injured, like he had a real ankle issue. I have seen him in the locker room a couple times, he was limping and everything. Mitch Johnson said this is one of the guys who, even if he is injured, he is going to play anyway, he does not complain. This is who De'Aaron Fox is, first of all. Second of all, I think if you see the five first games of the season right now, he is one of the best Spurs players. I think he is bouncing back crazy. To answer your question about the locker room, he is so important in the locker room. He is one of the main guys, he is one of the only vets as well.
quotes.social_post: De'Aaron Fox is bouncing back strong after playing through a significant ankle injury during the finals. Maxime Aubin calls him one of the best Spurs players through the first five games.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin discusses De'Aaron Fox's recovery from an ankle injury and his importance to the Spurs locker room.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs face long-term salary cap challenges with their core
quotes.excerpt: you are going to have to pay Carter, you are going to have to pay Harper
quotes.quote: If you are the Spurs front office, you do not really have a choice right now. He has a big contract. You have to say that you trust him for now. We will see in the future, because I think everybody is asking the same questions and they are right to ask it. How can you keep them long-term? Because one day you are going to have to pay Carter, you are going to have to pay Harper. Fox has already a huge salary, Wembanyama next year is going to have a big one as well. So, you have to already think two years and three years from now. But if we just talk about this season, I think they want the best version of Fox. I think they trust him, and I think so far he has been doing amazing.
quotes.social_post: The Spurs face long-term salary cap questions as they look to retain their core. Maxime Aubin notes the front office must plan for future extensions for Carter, Harper, and Wembanyama.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin discusses the long-term salary cap challenges the Spurs front office faces regarding their core players.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' core players have a genuine chemistry
quotes.excerpt: it seems to me like they are so smart for a team and they genuinely like each other
quotes.quote: It seems to me like they are so smart for a team and they genuinely like each other, and it makes me think it is going to work at some point, these three guys together. But to come back to media day, it did not say to us, but it was funny, because coming back to that day, I think it was September 29th or something, we all arrived at the Spurs training facility, and there is a GQ interview going on and on. And that was Harper and Carter deciding to do something together. And I think it was not the best idea for them to do that, because it was just the two of them and the title was something like, this is the new generation of the Spurs, this is the two new guards of San Antonio. Okay, where is Fox in that? And so the GQ interview, I read the whole thing and this is in the GQ interview, Harper says basically, no, I am not going off the bench or something like that. But he is joking about it, once again, I do not want to, you know, he is joking about it, but still saying it.
quotes.social_post: Maxime Aubin discusses the chemistry between the Spurs' young core, noting that while they genuinely like each other, managing roles and egos remains a key storyline for the team.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin reflects on the chemistry between Spurs players and a specific GQ interview involving the team's guards.
